newTerms.gracefulness / graciousness: elegancia de las formas / gracia en el trato

forcedChoices.reason: Followers address Jesus with tú throughout; the 'Oriental potentate' manner describes her approach, not a form of address.

forcedChoices.choice: Servants speak to their lord with «usted»; the lord answers with «tú»
forcedChoices.reason: Packet rule: great respect to a ruler takes usted; the lord speaks down to a servant.

forcedChoices.choice: «you» after the lament over Jerusalem kept singular (desearás, me buscarás)
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces number; the addressee of the preceding sentences is the city, so the singular keeps the same addressee.
The sentence depends on one verb for both the rising of the Son of Man and the 'rising of the kingdom'; «resucitar» would break the link.
«zorra» has a vulgar sense in many countries that the authors did not intend.

forcedChoices.choice: gracefulness = «elegancia de las formas», graciousness = «gracia en el trato»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish «gracia» covers both English words; qualifiers keep the contrast while «gracia» stays linked to «grace» and «gracious» in 171:7.1-7.2.
Spanish needs different prepositions; the emphasis stays on the prepositions as in English.
Three distinct English words in one paragraph need three distinct forms; follows earlier-paper term choices.
